findings.title: Psalm 136:25 has no English but shares Psalm 136:24’s English alignment row
findings.evidence: In both actual scratch compiler outputs, the p:parallel row containing Hebrew verse milestones 136/24 and 136/25 has English verse milestone 136/24 with “And He rescued us from our enemies” and its refrain. The next separate row is v.26. The whole-psalm recipe call therefore does not keep the absent translation structurally isolated, despite no extra English words being invented. Source scan61-band1 has neither the giving-food line nor its refrain. First-day spec lines 760–765 explicitly solved this same verified omission with three bounded calls.
findings.required_change: Keep the literal chapter witnesses and the Hebrew canonical v.25, but call the bilingual 1–24 range, Hebrew-only v.25, and bilingual v.26 separately in documentary and expanded recitation order. Ensure v.25 gets no English donor, placeholder, inherited alignment or provenance, and prevent automatic range override against the end. Recompile both modes and assert independent rows and intact 26 HE / 25 EN refrains.

resolution.evidence: Final compact range ends /136/24, with canonical v.25 and v.26 as separate calls. Ran actual prospective data through the documentary and expanded section compilers in a scratch refdb. Indexed the other-volume Marmorstein and JPS Psalm 136 providers as real unselected competitors. Both outputs have exact verses 1–24 and 26 paired by verse, exactly one Hebrew line at v.25, and 26 Hebrew / 25 English semantic refrains. The documentary empty English structural wrapper has neither words nor page links and is not an encoded English witness. Expanded output has no English item at v.25. Both preserve 19 citation notes.
